answer_summary: Intended qualitative choices: 1-c (A switches to B), 2-d (B switches to A), 3-b (Process B is prolonged), 4-e (oscillations stop). The Lean development derives [Br-]_critical = 3/10000000 M from the printed step-(1)/step-(4) rates and proves mechanistic certificates for all four choices. Pulse-threshold and feed-invariance qualifications are stated explicitly because their magnitudes are not printed.
assumptions: Positive HBrO2 and H+ concentrations permit cancellation of their common factors in the printed elementary rate laws.
The printed elementary reactions obey their mass-action rate laws; this is also the rate comparison explicitly requested by the problem.
As a trusted general chemistry law, added Ag+ removes dissolved Br- through AgBr(s) precipitation.
For action 3, the remaining time to the critical boundary is strictly increasing with the starting Br- concentration along the stated monotone Process-B segment; no constant-speed assumption is used.
For the intended action-4 response, continuous Br- input maintains Br- above its critical concentration.
source_gaps: The phrase 'small amount' gives no Ce4+ or Ag+ dose. Immediate choices c and d require a threshold-crossing perturbation; a smaller pulse only advances the eventual switch.
The continuous Br- feed rate is not specified. Choice e requires input sufficient to prevent Br- from falling to the critical value; an insufficient feed need not stop oscillations.
